claims.text: Traditional EAM references are unable to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid.
Replacing an EAM reference with an adaptive ML-IAP trained on ab initio liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed replacement will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch in both solid and liquid high-entropy alloys near their melting temperatures.
The ML-IAP should be trained on a diverse set of ab initio molecular-dynamics snapshots of the liquid state.
Including corresponding disordered-solid configurations in training may extend the reference to the solid state.
The proposed method applies to alloys containing three to seven major components, with each component present at 10–40 at%.
The applicable temperature range is approximately 0.8–1.0 times the melting temperature.
Liquid-like dynamics are prevalent over the stated 0.8–1.0 T_m range.
An ML-IAP trained on diverse ab initio configurations can capture complex many-body interactions.
An ML-IAP trained on diverse ab initio configurations can capture multicomponent interactions.
Capturing many-body interactions and configurational diversity will produce closer overlap with the ab initio configuration phase space.
The trained ML-IAP will represent the liquid-state energy landscape more accurately than conventional EAM potentials.
A more accurate representation of the liquid-state energy landscape will reduce discrepancy along the thermodynamic-integration path.
The ML-IAP will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by at least 50% relative to TOR-TILD's conventional EAM reference.
The proposed benefit depends on having sufficiently diverse and representative ab initio training data.
The hypothesis may not transfer to systems beyond three to seven components or to temperatures substantially outside 0.8–1.0 T_m.
The proposed quantitative improvement is extrapolated from elemental and binary cases.
